references.text: Moses gives the same exhortation to Joshua: "Be strong and courageous," in connection with the transition to the promised land.
Moses says directly to Joshua that he must be strong and courageous, for he will lead the people into the land that the Lord promised their fathers.
The Lord Himself gives Joshua the command to be strong and courageous, with a promise to lead the people into the promised land.
The same exhortation is repeated to Joshua: "Be strong and courageous," with assurance of the Lord's presence.
Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh give the same encouragement to Joshua: "Be strong and courageous."
God's promise to Abraham to give his descendants the land of Canaan, here referred to as the promise to the fathers.
God's oath to Isaac to give his offspring all these lands, a confirmation of the promise to the fathers.
God's promise to Jacob to give him and his descendants the land, which is the promise to be fulfilled through Joshua.
Encouragement to be bold and courageous based on the Lord's promise never to leave or forsake, reflecting the promise given to Joshua.
